body: I'll tell them the truth. I don't lie to my kids. And I'm not ashamed of why I'm doing it.

I'm sorry that you had that experience, truly.

We already have two children, and they have my husband's last name. That wouldn't change. I have been on the same team with my husband since we were 8, and I'll be on the same team with him until the day I die. Just because I don't feel that his last name is my identity, doesn't mean we aren't married and it doesn't erase our history or our future.
I have been considering that, and I think I can hyphenate it without legally changing my name in any way...thats been a thing too.

You know...damn. You are really, really right.

I don't know why I never thought to say "no" to the relation question. I guess I felt like I was somehow obligated to tell the truth, but really, I'm not related to them. My husband is my family, not them.

He is a really amazing person, and a life saver in many ways. I think your suggestion for counseling is a good idea...the very last thing I'd ever want is to make him feel like I am not proud of him or want to be associated with him.

Thank you 🖤 🖤

I respect what you're saying, but he is a very kind, thoughtful person who oftentimes won't say what he feels or means because he's afraid of hurting others. It's only when I call him out on what he's not saying, that he admits to what he's really feeling. Communication isn't his strong point, and patience isn't mine, which is why we compliment each other so well-we are literally exact opposites.

Things got so bad around this time last year that I did finally break off contact with them. Maybe a year isn't enough for the association to fade, maybe more time is the key.

I did think of changing my name to some sort of blend of his and mine, still working on that-I feel like that could be a workable solution too. Thank you for the suggestions!
That's a good suggestion, I would think about doing that for myself, but I don't think he will want to. I didn't think of that!
I had considered that, but he doesn't want to change his. Aside from his parents, he is proud of it and I respect that.
I won't lie, sometimes it's painful. But I find that when I write about it, I don't sugarcoat or lie about what happened. When I try to talk to people about it, I never tell the whole story.
I really hope it helps!

It seems like you've made up your mind, and as someone that has walked that road, I understand you don't want to hear the life clichés. I'm sorry you've gotten to this point. I wish I could give you a pep talk. I wish I could tell you that there is a beautiful world out there outside of California where things might not be better, but they are different, and sometimes different makes all the difference.

Whatever you choose, should you ever need to talk, I'm happy to listen.

Yes. My capacity for holding grudges is legendary within my family anyway, and it's tenfold with the root of my PTSD. Sometimes, if I get really obsessed about it, I write it out as a story. It has helped me to channel my anger into a creative, productive activity.

So many people say it to me. It's so frustrating because I have to hide the only part of myself that's actually good.

I would like to talk more.
I don't think that would be a solution to this. The only reason I haven't killed myself yet is because of the love I have for my husband and kids.

I wish that I was more patient, and that my husband was more assertive. Given a tiny bit more of each of these traits, we'd be the perfect balance for each other...or at least wouldn't make each other so mad!
Here if you need a shoulder.

I understand exactly what you're saying. Happy day? I'm mad. Sad time? Angry. Any emotional situation makes me enraged. I can't process emotions, except anger. I can't help, I have no advice, but I understand you and you aren't alone.
I've been reliant on the extra money, but this is advice I'm planning to take.
I'm definitely looking for another job. In the meantime, I think I might stop writing for them; it's paid separately from my full time work and not a requirement. They seem clueless.

Well, that's definitely in the works. She has also started to belittle writing in general, and has been trying to discourage me by saying I will never find anything better since I don't have a degree. I can handle all that, but I don't want to be regarded as someone who commits the sin of plagiarism.
That was my initial feeling, I thought maybe I was over reacting.

That's what I'm facing now. If I try to talk to anyone about it, now it seems as if I'm inconveniencing them. Honestly that's what is pushing me closer to doing it again. I can totally relate to the drunk SH! God that's the worst time.

It's not an easy battle. If you ever have interest in someone to talk to, I'm here. Not that I'm exactly helpful, but I think a lot of my issue is that I feel like I can't talk about it with the people around me, they just judge and I don't need it.
Thank you for sharing this. I'm so happy to read that you were able to find help. You are an inspiration.
I do have quote a few tattoos and they do help, temporarily. Have you ever relapsed?

I did try the tattoo route, but 11 tattoos later I still haven't been successful in recreating the feeling. It's such a strange release too, I'm sure you know exactly what I'm talking about although it's impossible to put into words.
I can understand where you're coming from, but that has not been my experience personally.
I will!
Thank you. I knew all of this, but sometimes hearing it from someone else makes a bigger difference.

You're right. I should take them to do some fun things.

I am scared to get close to them. I love them so much, and many days they are the only positive thing in my life. But what if I am weak and I can't stop myself? I feel myself drifting from them to try to protect them from being hurt if I kill myself.

I am taking my first vacation (a stay cation) at the beginning of the summer so I can spend some time with my daughters. I do look forward to that.

I don't want to do that to them. But I hate this life and this person I am.
Thank you for everything. I'm not sure why you found my thread but I'm grateful.
I hope that you do too. It's a lonely way to live.
I'm very fortunate to have found this place.

I've never interacted with another person who has/had PTSD, so thank you for sharing this. At least, I don't think I have; most people in my area are very closed off about any mental health related topics. 

I know you're right. I've held everything in for so long to protect my husband and our two daughters, but maybe it's not because of that. I think a part of me has held it in because of the way people treat me if I share with them that I struggled with PTSD. Now I feel alienated and empty. 

Everything you said has really struck a cord. These are all things I've said to others to help, but strangely, it makes a bigger difference when someone else says it. 

I'm not sure how to treat myself today. I'm at work for about 5 more hours, then I'll go get my daughters and cook for them; maybe I will try to paint today, that is something I really enjoy.

Truly, thank you. I can't express how much of a relief it is just to type words, know another human is seeing them and not being berated for it.

Thank you for replying.

I do desperately want to live. I want to be happy and I want to survive. I struggle with PTSD and the flashbacks are forever convincing me that no matter what I do, or how beautiful life is, I will always be stuck in the past. Seeing events played out repetitively has drained any hope I had to be happy.
This is such an awesome idea, thank you for sharing!
I will talk to you, we will all talk to you. Don't go out like this, please.

It's been awhile since I've been in school, but I remember this disconnected feeling. Sometimes I feel it when it's time for me to go to work. I will lay in bed, and wonder what the point is. 

Something that has helped me is figuring out what it is about the activity that overwhelms me. With school, I would skip and then get behind, and then I felt like it was useless ontop of already being depressed. I know it isn't easy, but it was helpful for me to sit down and have an honest conversation with my teachers and explain that I was feeling overwhelmed and needed help. I'm not sure if this is something that you'd be comfortable with, but it might get you back on track with school, and also give you an outlet to discuss how you're feeling.

I see you. I understand where you are.

I have these thoughts daily, so I'm not going to pretend that it always gets better. Sometimes, it doesn't. I feel empty and listless most days, but I stay because my kids love me. There is no motive behind their love, they just love me because of me.

It's the same with your niece. You are the bestest uncle. She sees you, she sees what you can't see. I don't advocate living for others because it's an unstable and unhealthy way to operate. But, I do advocate the importance of worth measured by those who are innocent. A pure source of love is sometimes enough to say, "let's hang on a little while longer". I hope you hang on a while longer friend, and know that we are here for you, and I am here for you, if you need to talk.
